data_date: Listed Buildings polygons last updated 2026-09-11 on Historic England Open Data page; ArcGIS layer data last edit 2026-09-01T05:47:56Z
dataset: National Heritage List for England (NHLE) - Listed Building polygons

field_evidence.building_semantics: Historic England states Listed Buildings can include structures such as railings, gate piers, walls, war memorials, gravestones, post boxes and telephone boxes. Thus Listed Building status alone is not accepted as proof of a physical building.
field_evidence.footprint: The official layer is polygon geometry, but no record-level payload was retrieved and Historic England describes NHLE polygons as designation/map polygons rather than guaranteeing every polygon is a physical building footprint. Therefore polygon metadata alone is not accepted as a footprint record.
field_evidence.record_payload: No <=50 Exeter-bbox GeoJSON feature payload bytes were obtained through the available public retrieval surface.
field_evidence.type_use: The official layer schema contains designation/name/grade/date/location fields but no explicit current building use/type field. Name or Grade are not treated as use classifications.

first_missing_criterion: official record-level feature where Polygon/MultiPolygon is explicitly the physical building footprint and the same record carries an evidence-bearing building type/use field. Historic England NHLE layer 3 is an official listed-building polygon layer, but its schema exposes ListEntry/Name/Grade/date/location fields rather than current use/type, and NHLE 'Listed Buildings' can include non-building structures; the <=50 Exeter-bbox feature payload was not retrievable through the available public fetch surface.
